original_source: William Lilly, Christian Astrology (1647), Wellcome first edition b30338724
title: Whether the Native shall be Rich
documentation_scope: Lilly's conditional historical economic forecasts; NOT validated human wealth or financial decision guidance

source_groups.source_topic: Numbered wealth chapter heading and dependence on the unnumbered source selection

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: CHAP CXIIII Whether the Native shall be Rich
claims.historical_only_meaning: A new numbered chapter starts below a horizontal rule on original PDF frame587, after the unnumbered second-house wealth introduction.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: all the Significators ... constituted so as aforesaid
claims.historical_only_meaning: The chapter deliberately reuses the significators defined immediately above, rather than supplying an independent or different wealth-selection universe.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: in angles
claims.historical_only_meaning: Angular placement of all the wealth significators is offered as a favorable configuration within a larger multi-factor rule.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: or the greater part of them
claims.historical_only_meaning: The author also accepts the greater part, rather than all, of the wealth significators being angular; no numerical proportion beyond that phrase.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: and be also essentially dignified
claims.historical_only_meaning: Essential dignity is required in addition to the angular-placement condition for the large-estate conclusion.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: very great Estate
claims.historical_only_meaning: Under the preceding conjunctive conditions the source asserts attainment of a substantial estate, without independent wealth observations.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: plenty of all things ... necessitated in nothing
claims.historical_only_meaning: Lilly characterizes the imagined prosperous state as abundance and absence of want; this is an outcome interpretation, not another independent test.

source_groups.source_topic: Significator testimony count, degrees of fortune, poverty and moderation

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: more testimonies ... fortitudes or debilities
claims.historical_only_meaning: The number of contrary strength/weakness testimonies is said to determine the degree of wealth or poverty; no numerical calibration or weighting scheme is specified.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: greatnesse or weaknesse of the Estate
claims.historical_only_meaning: The author treats economic outcome magnitude as variable and graded rather than strictly rich versus poor.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: all the Significators weak, argue poverty
claims.historical_only_meaning: The all-weak-significator state is an explicit unfavorable branch, not an absence of the favorable branch alone.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: if moderately fortified
claims.historical_only_meaning: Moderately fortified significators form a third category between extreme wealth and poverty.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: the Native shall not exceed or want
claims.historical_only_meaning: The intermediate branch predicts neither great abundance nor deprivation; the implied socioeconomic thresholds are undefined.

source_groups.source_topic: Fixed star/benefic sentence and no mandatory benefic category

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: or with Regulus
claims.historical_only_meaning: The Regulus clause follows the moderate-fortification sentence; its exact governing antecedent/operator scope is unclear from the printed syntax.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: or Spica Virgo
claims.historical_only_meaning: Spica is separately named with a Virgo glyph/epithet, but exact orb, aspect and grammatical connection to the wealth result are unstated.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: or the Fortunes in good houses of Heaven
claims.historical_only_meaning: The beneficial planets occupying good houses appear as an additional condition; do not silently apply it to every significator.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: no matter ... Fortunes or Infortunes
claims.historical_only_meaning: The author explicitly states that wealth significators need not be benefic by planetary category; disposition and other testimony matter more.

source_groups.source_topic: Cross-page Sun and Moon abundance claim

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Aboundance of Estate ... the two Lights
claims.historical_only_meaning: The abundance claim has the Sun and Moon as joint subject, across the first-edition page boundary 587–588.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: are with eminent fixed Starres
claims.historical_only_meaning: The Sun and Moon with prominent fixed stars is an asserted positive outcome source, requiring a separate frozen definition of 'with'.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: or the Fortunes
claims.historical_only_meaning: The author gives beneficial planets as an alternative to the fixed stars, not an additional requirement to every light/star configuration.

source_groups.source_topic: First listed sign of wealth: Moon in Ascendant

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Moon in the ascendant fortunate
claims.historical_only_meaning: A favorably placed Moon at the Ascendant is said to predict wealth and esteem; its favourable-state qualifier is essential.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: giveth Wealth and estimation all the life long
claims.historical_only_meaning: The author attaches prolonged wealth and recognition to the qualified Ascendant Moon, with no independently documented lifelong follow-up.

source_groups.source_topic: Sun-Moon trine with solar exaltation and non-affliction

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Sun and Moon in Trine
claims.historical_only_meaning: Trine aspect of the luminaries is one component of this special wealth testimony, not a standalone sufficient condition.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Sun then in his Exaltation
claims.historical_only_meaning: The Sun's exaltation is an additional condition on the luminary trine, not a property of every trine.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: neither of them unfortunated by Saturn or Mars
claims.historical_only_meaning: The author also requires neither luminary to be harmed by Saturn or Mars, a contrary-testimony veto.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: ample testimonies of a large Fortune
claims.historical_only_meaning: The compound luminary configuration allegedly supports large fortune; no economic outcome or prediction accuracy was measured.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Jupiter in the second and Moon in the first
claims.historical_only_meaning: One alternative is Jupiter in the second house and Moon in the first, with no explicit shared-sign dignity requirements in this first alternative.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: or Jupiter in the ascendant in his owne dignities
claims.historical_only_meaning: The second alternative places Jupiter in the Ascendant and explicitly requires Jupiter's own dignity; this must not leak into the first alternative.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Moon in the second in her dignities
claims.historical_only_meaning: The second alternative also places the Moon in the second in her dignity; it is conjunctive with the second Jupiter condition.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: promises Wealth
claims.historical_only_meaning: These two alternatives form a historical claimed wealth rule, not independent prediction confirmations.

source_groups.source_topic: Conditional inheritances: Saturn and eighth-house configurations

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Saturn in a diurnall Geniture in the eighth
claims.historical_only_meaning: Saturn in the eighth in a daytime nativity is a prerequisite of this particular inheritance-from-death claim.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: in aspect with either of the Fortunes
claims.historical_only_meaning: Saturn in that setting must aspect at least one beneficial planet; the historical outcome is not implied merely by Saturn in the eighth.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: obtains a Fortune by the death of persons
claims.historical_only_meaning: The source claims that the specified condition can produce an estate by a deceased person, with no documented forecast validation.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Lord of the eighth is fortunate ... essential dignities
claims.historical_only_meaning: The ruler of the eighth house in essential dignity provides another potential inheritance branch.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: placed in the tenth house
claims.historical_only_meaning: The eighth-house ruler in the tenth is an additional placement requirement of that branch.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: acquire an Estate by the deceased
claims.historical_only_meaning: The second branch also links death/inheritance to financial gain, but without specifying a genuine predicted person or date.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Lord of Part of Fortune is in the eighth
claims.historical_only_meaning: A third branch begins with the ruler of Part of Fortune being located in the eighth house.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Lord of the ascendant aspects him
claims.historical_only_meaning: This third branch also requires aspect from the Ascendant ruler to the Part of Fortune's ruler, not necessarily to Part of Fortune itself.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Wealth comes by dead Folkes
claims.historical_only_meaning: The third inheritance statement is a distinct configuration with the same unvalidated outcome category.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Saturn is well posited
claims.historical_only_meaning: A well-situated Saturn is the first requirement of this alleged land/estate accumulation configuration.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: and essentially strong
claims.historical_only_meaning: Saturn's essential dignity is an additional requirement; do not substitute it for general placement quality.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: aspects the ascendant with a Trine
claims.historical_only_meaning: The angular relationship is explicitly Saturn trine to Ascendant, not a generic Saturn influence.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: rich by Lands Orchards Fields and Pastures
claims.historical_only_meaning: Lilly claims wealth from landed assets under these joint conditions, without any independent contemporary economic data.

source_groups.source_topic: Poverty configurations from Moon/Mars and Saturn

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Moon in conjunction with Mars with Saturn in any angle
claims.historical_only_meaning: The author makes a severe poverty assertion under combined Moon, Mars and angular Saturn conditions; precise Saturn/Mars grammatical attachment should be audited.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: though a King ... reduced to poverty
claims.historical_only_meaning: The historical text makes a high-confidence reversal claim even for a wealthy ruler, but gives no independent example or quantified probability.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: the Square of Saturn and Moon
claims.historical_only_meaning: A square aspect of Saturn/Moon is presented as an estate-destruction indicator; this is a negative, not merely an absence of benefic evidence.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: or Opposition of Saturn and Moon
claims.historical_only_meaning: An opposition of Saturn/Moon is the alternative to the square, separately preserved.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: destroys the Estate
claims.historical_only_meaning: The source links those aspects to losing an estate, but does not provide time windows or independent financial evidence.

source_groups.source_topic: Other alternative conditions alleging financial ruin

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Infortunes in angles and Fortunes in succedant
claims.historical_only_meaning: The malefics angular and benefics in succedent houses are jointly described as an adverse wealth configuration.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: or Moon combust
claims.historical_only_meaning: Combust Moon is given as another negative branch in the complex poverty sentence.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: her Dispositor infortunate
claims.historical_only_meaning: The combust-Moon branch also includes an afflicted lunar dispositor; exact conjunction with other negative branches must be preserved.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: place of the [uncertain glyphs] oppressed
claims.historical_only_meaning: The text names a hard-to-resolve zodiacal/planetary glyph place oppressed by malefics, and the original symbolic referent remains explicitly unresolved.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: they cadent ... Lord thereof being an Infortune and strong
claims.historical_only_meaning: The cadent condition plus malefic lord of the named place appears in the poverty cluster; 'they' and 'thereof' referents require a close reading.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: or Jupiter cadent and his Dispositor not potent
claims.historical_only_meaning: Another branch requires Jupiter cadent and its dispositor lacking strength, not simply cadent Jupiter.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: from a vast Estate ... great want
claims.historical_only_meaning: Under the cluster the author alleges reversal from substantial fortune to want, not a tested estimate of its frequency.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: and so the contrary
claims.historical_only_meaning: The source closes with an inverse-case expression whose exact mapping of all the foregoing conditions remains ambiguous.

source_groups.source_topic: Distinct following chapter on sources of wealth; record navigation only

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: CHAP CXV From whence or by what meanes
claims.historical_only_meaning: Printed CXV begins below horizontal line in the lower part of PDF588 and continues on PDF589; it is separate from whether-rich.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: nature of the Significators ... in what houses posited
claims.historical_only_meaning: Only the opening of the next method is noted as source navigation. Its detailed planet/person/matter table begins PDF589 and is not ingested here.
